title: lint: every save-door advisory rule carries a localized user sentence (67 rule ids in 36 rule files remain after the security posture), per ruling C on #32440
body:
domain:spec#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgU7jN46DmQ6XFvz28s

Filing gate: ④ a coordination node. This is the tracking card for the per-domain sub-cards below. It sits under tracking #32654 and continues layer 1 (#32655) of the ruling's scope.
Business reason: maintainer ruling 「32440 选C，32043 一起按C处理」 (ruling record 6819749037, option C of analysis 6819513436) says the server returns localized advisory text in the request's language and the rule id stays the same. #32655 (PR #32790) delivers the contract and the first producer, the security posture linter's 7 advisory rule ids in all 11 platform locales. Every other advisory the save and publish doors return still has no user sentence. Once layer 2 (#32656) composes `userMessage` and layer 3 (#32657) renders it, a user saving in a zh-Hans, ja or ar Studio gets their own language for 7 rules and the declared English fallback for the other 67.
Reader who acts: the `domain:spec` seat dispatches each sub-card. The implementer edits `packages/lint` only: a `RULE_FILE.user-text.ts` catalog beside each rule file, `userTextParams` at its push sites, and the merge into `FINDING_USER_TEXT_CATALOG`.
Dedupe words: `userTextParams`, `user-text.ts catalog`, `findingUserMessage`, `advisory localized user sentence`.

Back-link: #32655 · parent #32654 · ⛔ Not a claim. Grading is triage's.

## Scope (measured)

The #32655 developer measured this at `9925cc13` (report 6823397904 on #32655) with a static scan. The scan took the `AUTHORING_RULES` entries that carry `runtime-publish` (38 of 65), followed their import closure (91 files), and collected the finding literals whose severity is `warning` or `info`. The result is 74 lint rule ids that the save door can return as advisories. #32655 covers 7 of them (`validate-security-posture.ts`), and **67 remain, in 36 rule files**. None of those 36 files changed between `fa1134c6` and `main` `88282a78`.

The count is an upper bound. The import closure over-approximates which ids a runtime-publish entry emits, and 4 constants from other packages were counted even though the script did not resolve them. Each sub-card re-measures its own files before it writes anything.

`metadata-protocol`'s own gate-local advisories are not in this scope: `public-form-intake-unavailable`, the draft-time hierarchy-scope warning, the html-page compile warnings and the storage-refused notice. Their producer is layer 2 (#32656).

## Sub-cards (one per domain, so each lane keeps its terms consistent)

| Sub-card | Rule files | Rule ids |
|---|---|---|
| A1 automation writes (approval, flow, hook, action, email) | 11 | 27 |
| A2 dashboards, charts and widgets | 3 | 11 |
| A3 data model (object, field, sort, search, title, autonumber) | 6 | 10 |
| A4 pages, forms, navigation and translations | 8 | 9 |
| A5 AI, connectors, mappings and sharing | 8 | 10 |
| **Total** | **36** | **67** |

## The pattern every sub-card follows (already in place, landed by #32655)

- A catalog `packages/lint/src/RULE_FILE.user-text.ts` sits beside its rule file. It is keyed by the rule's own id constant and has one sentence per rule id in every platform locale (`PLATFORM_LOCALE_TAGS`, 11 tags). `en` is required by the type. `validate-security-posture.user-text.ts` is the reference.
- Each advisory push site sets `userTextParams` to the names its sentence interpolates. The rule ids, `message` and `hint` stay unchanged.
- The catalog is merged into `FINDING_USER_TEXT_CATALOG` (`finding-user-text.ts`, `mergeUserTextCatalogs`, which refuses a rule id that two catalogs both claim).
- The pins follow `finding-user-text.test.ts`: the catalog holds exactly the file's advisory ids, each in exactly the 11 locales; every push site is rendered from the rule's real findings in every locale, with no `undefined` and no English stand-in; and one runtime-gate case shows a `userMessage` that `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema` parses.
- A sentence states only what the rule found. Where a rule reports part of a setting (the field-mask rule reports the inert half of a restriction), the push site carries that part in the params and the sentence has one arm per value, as `security-superuser-field-mask-inert` does with `inert`.
- Run `node scripts/check-cli-command-ids.mjs` after editing a catalog. It reads any source string segment that opens with "os " as an `os` CLI command, and Portuguese and Spanish lines hit it (twice on #32655's pt-BR lines). It is a CI lint step and is not in `dispatch-gates --commands`.
- The sentence is addressed to the person who saved the metadata in Studio. It uses the console's own terms (`ui/packages/i18n`) and says what the setting does and the one change that fixes it.
- No spec change is needed, because `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema.userMessage` already exists. The declaration lines are the dispatching seat's claim to set. The expected reading is `Metadata-protocol: none` with `@objectstack/lint` at `patch`, since the diff moves no authorable-surface shard.

## Done when

All five sub-cards have landed, and a re-run of the scan finds no runtime-publish advisory id without a catalog entry. Alternatively, the remaining ids are each named with the reason they stay on the English fallback.
